text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

text: RESULTS: Inspection: Noticeable swelling in the right knee. No other swellings or deformities noted elsewhere. Palpation: Swelling is warm to touch, without overlying skin redness or signs of local infection. Ultrasound_Knee: Compatible with hemarthrosis of the right knee, no evidence of fracture or dislocation. Complete_Blood_Count: Hemoglobin: 12.2 g/dL, Hematocrit: 36%, Leukocyte_count: 7,300/mm3, Platelet_count: 200,000/mm³. speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound confirms hemarthrosis, and the prolonged ACT with normal PT and PTT suggests a coagulation factor deficiency or inhibitor rather than platelet dysfunction. Given the family history and the specific lab profile, I am ready to conclude.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A
